question: Which of the following Government of India Acts of British India proposed the All India Federation (Federation of India)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1935**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of Indian Act was passed by the British parliament in 1935 and came into effect in 1937.
 
• The creation of a ‘Federation of India’ that consisted of two levels: a central executive and parliament, and below it, provinces and princely states.
 
• It discarded the ‘dyarchy’ system at the provincial level and allowed for the emergence of popularly elected provincial legislatures.
 
 
• Dyarchy was introduced at the central level, key subjects like defense and foreign affairs were under the direct control of the Governor-General.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Other Acts
 
• Government of India, Act, 1934 is the legislative act under the Reserve Bank of India.
 
 
• This act along with the Companies Act, which was amended in 1936, was meant to provide a framework for the supervision of banking firms in India.
 
 
 
• Government of India Act, 1919 was also known as Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
 
 
• It came into force in 1921.
 
• It was instituted in the British Indian polity to introduce the Diarchy, i.e., rule of two which means executive councilors and popular ministers.
 
• Dyarchy was introduced as a constitutional reform by Edwin Samuel Montagu, secretary of state for India (1917–22), and Lord Chelmsford, Viceroy of India (1916–21).
 
 
 
• Government of India Act, 1923, the Official Secrets Act 1923 is India's anti-espionage act held over from the British colonial period.
 
 
• The Official Secrets Act prohibits the disclosure of official documents and information and the wrongful communication of information that is considered sensitive by the government.
